description: Electric kiln ramp/hold/soak firing schedules, sourced from Digitalfire ahead of the site's shutdown. Complements data/firing/woodfire_schedules.json, which covers wood/reduction kilns only.

electric_schedules.name: Cone 6 Drop-and-Hold Slow Cool
electric_schedules.description: Plainsman cone 6 drop-and-hold, slow-cool schedule for reactive/glossy glazes. Improves brilliance and surface quality, reduces pinholing, and encourages microcrystal development in mattes.

steps.notes: Drop-and-hold: fast drop from peak, then hold
Slow cool through the glaze-stiffening range

electric_schedules.notes: The drop-and-hold at step 4 lets the melt level and heal bubbles before the slow-cool step encourages surface quality and matte crystal development. Applicable as a general template for any reactive or matte cone 6 glaze prone to pinholing or dull surface.

electric_schedules.name: Quartz Inversion Safe Cooling
electric_schedules.description: Not a full schedule - a rule of thumb to prevent dunting/cracking, applicable to any cone/body. Insert a slow ramp on both heating and cooling through the quartz inversion point.
guidance: Slow the ramp approaching and departing 570C/1063F in both directions - dunting risk exists on heat-up and cool-down
Most critical for thick, heavy, or unevenly-walled ware and for bodies with high free-quartz content
Electric kilns lack the natural draft of gas kilns and need slower firing overall to avoid gradients
Candle overnight at the boiling point before ramping up for damp or thick greenware
